subject: Re: LumenHealth vendor enrollment — MSA redline & PO routing gaps
messages:
From: Sarah Clark <sarah.clark@lumenhealth.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@lumenhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Vendor enrollment - MSA questions and PO routing

Rafael,

Thanks for the demo last week. We're ready to start enrollment in Ariba but hit two blockers on our side:

1) Our legal team reviewed the MSA and returned a set of redlines — they want a liability carveout for data egress which isn't in your latest doc.
2) Our shared services team says POs sent from Ariba are failing to map to our AP system unless the PO lines include the 'buyerCostCenter' custom field.

I've attached our W-9 and a SOC2 summary for vendor evidence. Can someone on your side confirm whether the MSA redline above is acceptable, and who owns the PO field mapping?

Regards,
Sarah Clark
Sr. Procurement Manager
LumenHealth
Attachments: Lumen_W9.pdf, SOC2_Type2_Summary.pdf

From: rafael.mendes@redwood.com
To: Sarah Clark <sarah.clark@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor enrollment - MSA questions and PO routing

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear summary and for sending the evidence. Looping in Marissa (legal) and Kimberly (commercial ops).

Short answers up front:
- We can review the liability carveout request; Marissa will respond with a proposed counter (or exception path) by EOD tomorrow.
- PO field mapping lives with our integration team (Karthik copied). We typically support a configurable 'custom field' mapping for buyerCostCenter but need an example XML payload to confirm alignment with your Ariba schema. The orderform-xml-sample will help.

Marissa / Karthik — can you take these two items? Sarah: if you can share a failing PO xml (redacted) that will speed triage.

Best,
Rafael
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com, Sarah Clark <sarah.clark@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-02T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor enrollment - MSA questions and PO routing

Thanks, Rafael. Sarah — I reviewed LumenHealth's requested MSA carveout. Key points from legal:

- The 'data egress' carveout as written would materially expand exposure. We can offer a limited exception: include explicit maximums for exfiltration (monetary cap) and require prior written notice + mitigation steps.
- We can also offer a shorter-term pilot amendment (90 days) with reporting requirements tied to any egress-related incidents.

I've attached a tracked-change doc (MSA_redline_RAFAEL_v4.docx) with two options: 'limited exception' and 'pilot amendment'. Please review and indicate preferred route. If Lumen prefers to proceed with the limited exception, we'll need a commercial approval for the cap (finance/leadership).

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
Attachments: MSA_redline_RAFAEL_v4.docx

From: Sarah Clark <sarah.clark@lumenhealth.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@lumenhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-02T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor enrollment - MSA questions and PO routing

Marissa — thanks for the quick read. Lumen prefers the 'pilot amendment' route so we can instrument and monitor for 90 days before a longer exception. Our procurement lead has asked for explicit data handling SLAs in that pilot text.

On the PO side: attached is a sanitized failing PO xml and a screenshot from Ariba showing the missing buyerCostCenter field. Can Karthik confirm whether Redwood's gateway can map a custom Ariba node to the internal 'costCenter' claim in our AP feed?

Sarah
Attachments: failing_po_example.xml

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com, Sarah Clark <sarah.clark@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-03T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor enrollment - PO routing / Ariba mapping

Sarah — thanks for the sample. We can map a custom Ariba node to buyerCostCenter, but two practical notes:

1) The mapping is performed at enrollment time and persisted on the vendor profile — we need a one-time instruction from Lumen specifying the XML path (e.g. /Order/BuyerCustomFields/BuyerCostCenter).
2) If the field is sometimes empty in PO feeds, we fall back to the vendor default cost center; that can reintroduce mapping failures for line-level validation.

Action items for go-forward:
- Lumen: confirm the exact xml path and whether the buyerCostCenter is guaranteed on every PO.
- Redwood: we'll add a mapping rule to the vendor record and run a test transmission.

I'll schedule a short mapping call — proposed: Wed 11/4 11:00 AM PT. Rafael / Kimberly — can one of you join for the commercial handoff?

Thanks,
Karthik
Integrations Lead, Redwood Inference

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: Sarah Clark <sarah.clark@lumenhealth.com>, rafael.mendes@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-04T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor enrollment - MSA & PO routing (final)

Sarah — short update after internal sync:

- Legal sign-off path: Marissa's pilot amendment is acceptable to Redwood with the 90-day telemetry clause. We have a draft ready for signature; we'll send the DocuSign link after you confirm the commercial cap (suggested $50k cap for the pilot unless Lumen proposes otherwise).
- Integration: Karthik confirmed the mapping approach and will run the test with your sanitized PO once we receive the exact xml path.
- Next steps: Rafael will prepare a mutual action plan (MAP) that lists sign -> enrollment -> mapping test -> pilot start (90d). I'll include deadlines so your operations team can schedule time.

Please confirm the xml path and commercial cap and we'll proceed to send the DocuSign envelope and enable the vendor in the Ariba connector.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Operations, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0199
